problems.problem: The batch still carries the unrevised sentence, so both open faults stand. First, the appositive ‘a pot of boiling milk’ is not in Sāyaṇa’s words on 8.61.7 (सप्त ऋत्विजः एकां घर्मं दुहन्ति ...); it is Cowell’s explanation in note 1 of Wilson vol. 5, and in Sāyaṇa’s own comment on this hymn the pot is the mahāvīra (8.61.10 to 12) while gharma names the hot-milk rite (घर्मयागस्य, 8.61.12; अभिष्टवे घर्मदोहे after 8.61.6). The sentence thus folds a conduit’s gloss into Sāyaṇa with no hedge (revrefute ~2 and ~3 both refuted on this). Second, it alone of 32 sentences reads ‘Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.61.7’ instead of ‘Sāyaṇa, on 8.61.7’.
problems.fix: Midway through a hymn to Agni, the verse speaks in numbers; Sāyaṇa, on 8.61.7, reads the seven as priests milking the one gharma of the hot-milk rite, and two of them, the adhvaryu priests, as directing five others, the sacrificer among them. Relabel evidence note 1 as Cowell’s hand, not Wilson’s, and keep the Sanskrit apart from the English; rerun entry-check.

problems.problem: The plain sense is a garden path: ‘A hymn to Agni that bids the destroyers go wishes in every verse ...’ reads first as ‘go wishes’, and the reader must back up to find the main verb. The reading itself stands (शं शान्तिनिमित्तं, योः विषययोगजनितं, and अग्निरेव सर्वं करोति).
problems.fix: Set the relative clause off with commas: ‘A hymn to Agni, which bids the destroyers go, wishes in every verse that all the others die away; Sāyaṇa, on 8.39.4, ...’ and change nothing else; rerun entry-check.
